summary: 本轮增量检索发现 1 项自上次成功运行后首次公开且足够相关的新工作：`Dex-X`。它把人类视频、仿真中的接触补全和可部署的视触觉灵巧操作策略连接起来，直接面向多指灵巧手与手臂平台上的抓取和接触丰富工具使用，因此符合本追踪器的核心范围。
summary_en: This incremental pass found 1 newly public and sufficiently relevant item since the last successful run: `Dex-X`. It connects human videos, simulated contact completion, and deployable visual-tactile dexterous manipulation policies, directly targeting multi-finger hand-arm platforms for grasping and contact-rich tool use, so it fits the tracker’s core scope.

items.title: Dex-X: Learning Visual-Tactile Dexterous Manipulation From Human Videos with Simulated Interaction
items.authors_or_org: Ruoqu Chen, Feixiang Ruan, Liu Cao, Zihao Wang, Botian Xu, Shiqin Tong, Jiajun Liu, Mingzhi Pei, Chenyu Zhang, Wanli Xing, Kaifeng Zhang, Mengdi Xu
items.relevance: 该工作把灵巧操作、视触觉学习和多指手臂平台放在主线位置，目标是从人类视频学习可部署的灵巧操作策略，而不是泛化的视觉操控。
items.relevance_en: The work places dexterous manipulation, visual-tactile learning, and a multi-finger hand-arm platform at the center, aiming to learn deployable dexterous policies from human videos rather than generic vision-based manipulation.
items.novelty_signal: 2026-09-07 首次公开，提出仿真触觉补全与视频到可部署灵巧策略的完整路径，并给出真实机器人零样本迁移结果。
items.novelty_signal_en: First public on 2026-09-07, it proposes an end-to-end path from human videos to deployable dexterous policies via simulated tactile completion, with zero-shot real-robot transfer results.
items.analysis_zh: Dex-X 的主要工作是把人类视频转化为可部署的视触觉灵巧操作策略，解决的是灵巧操作中高质量示教稀缺、视频里缺少触觉信息、而真实机器人侧采集成本又很高的问题。其方法核心是把仿真当作“触觉补全引擎”：先从单目人类演示重建手物交互，再在物理一致的仿真接触动力学中生成原视频没有的触觉监督，随后训练视触觉策略，并蒸馏为可在点云和触觉输入上运行的部署策略。公开结果显示，它在多类抓取和接触丰富工具使用任务上实现了灵巧手臂平台的零样本 sim-to-real 迁移，教师策略在仿真中六类任务平均成功率为 65.9%，蒸馏后的策略在真实世界立方体抓取上达到 93%，在更难的桌面清理任务上达到 53%，并对未见几何体表现出一定泛化。总体上，这项工作把互联网视频与可执行灵巧控制连接起来，路线清晰且很有扩展性；限制在于当前公开信息主要来自摘要，关于重建误差、失败模式、消融设置和更广泛手型上的稳健性仍不充分。
items.analysis_en: Dex-X’s main contribution is a pipeline that turns human videos into deployable visual-tactile dexterous manipulation policies, addressing the lack of high-quality demonstrations, the absence of tactile signals in videos, and the high cost of collecting robot-side data. The key method is to use simulation as a “tactile completion engine”: the system reconstructs hand-object interaction from monocular human demonstrations, then leverages physically grounded contact dynamics in simulation to synthesize tactile supervision that is missing from the original videos. It then trains visual-tactile policies and distills them into deployable policies that run on point-cloud and tactile inputs. The public results report zero-shot sim-to-real transfer on a dexterous hand-arm platform across grasping and contact-rich tool-use tasks, with the teacher policy reaching 65.9% average success over six task categories in simulation, the distilled policy achieving 93% on real-world cube picking and 53% on the harder table-cleaning task, and some generalization to unseen object geometries. Overall, the work provides a clear and scalable bridge from internet video to executable dexterous control. The main limitation is that the public information is still mostly abstract-level, so reconstruction error, failure modes, ablation details, and robustness across broader hand embodiments remain under-specified.
